title: West Goshen votes Tuesday on a 10-year plan for its 14 parks
summary: The township's 2026-2035 Park, Recreation & Open Space plan goes to the Board of Supervisors for a public hearing and possible adoption, laying out playground upgrades, trail expansion and new sports facilities across 193 acres that will nearly double once the Greystone Preserve is added. One proposal would swap a use at Robert E. Lambert Park for pickleball courts, and some residents say the approval is moving too fast.

title: Neighbors raise $88K to restore Everhart Park's 1908 gazebo
summary: The Friends of Everhart Park are funding a restoration of the park's rustic cedar-and-fieldstone gazebo over Black Horse Run entirely through private donations, with about $55,000 of the $88,000 goal raised. Work starts with hand-shaped red cedar guardrails and refurbished benches, followed by a new rot-resistant shingle roof on the National Register-listed structure.

title: Rustin grad's nicotine step-down device is now in 70 UK pharmacies
summary: Zachary Starr founded Quix Labs at 16 after watching classmates at West Chester Rustin High School struggle with nicotine; now 23 and a 2024 West Chester University graduate, he sells its Quixotic refillable inhaler in roughly 70 pharmacies across England. The nine-person company kept its headquarters in West Goshen and is aiming to submit for FDA review by 2028.

title: 14 West Chester students named National Merit semifinalists
summary: Henderson High School led the area with seven semifinalists, followed by four at Pennsylvania Leadership Charter School, two at Rustin and one at East. The students now move on to the finalist round, with scholarship winners chosen next spring.

title: Inside the seven-week redo of Eagles linebacker Zack Baun's West Chester house
summary: Philadelphia Magazine toured the home Baun and his wife Ali bought last spring, furnished by Bryn Mawr designer Brittany Hakimfar of Far Studio on a seven-week deadline before the Eagles' preseason. The result leans organic modern: quiet colors, simple lines and heavy natural materials.

title: Helicopter museum honors the first piloted hydrogen-powered flight
summary: The American Helicopter Museum and Education Center is giving its 2026 Achievement Award to the Unither Bioelectronique and Robinson Helicopter team behind the first piloted flight of a hydrogen-powered helicopter, which drew about 90 percent of its energy from fuel cells. The award ceremony is set for Oct. 18 at the museum.

title: WCU opens its sustainability showcase to the public on Sept. 16
summary: West Chester University is inviting neighbors to a free showcase of its campus sustainability work Wednesday, Sept. 16 from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. in the Sykes Student Union ballrooms. Exhibits cover green roofs, recycling and waste reduction, responsible purchasing and sustainability education.

title: Spring freeze leaves Highland Orchards with a sliver of its apple crop
summary: After an April warm spell was followed by a hard freeze, Highland Orchards expects roughly 5 percent of a normal apple harvest, so pick-your-own will run shorter hours with far fewer varieties this fall. Hayrides, the corn maze and crops the freeze spared are still going ahead.

title: Community invited to greet Vietnam veterans returning from Honor Flight
summary: Saints Simon and Jude Parish hosts a Welcome Home celebration on Saturday, Sept. 19 for Vietnam veterans coming back from Honor Flight Philadelphia's Day of Honor in Washington. Activities start at 4 p.m. and the buses arrive around 6 p.m.; organizers are asking neighbors to line the entrance with flags.
loc: Saints Simon and Jude Parish, West Chester

title: A speakeasy-style barbershop opens down an alley off High Street
summary: Gerome and Monica Ruff have opened Urban Cutz Barbershop at 21 S. High Street, tucked behind Ginkgo Arts and reached through a covered brick walkway next to Barnaby's. Gerome has cut hair in the borough for more than 18 years; the couple plan to add chairs and more barbers as the 1,200-square-foot shop grows.
